chapter: Hippolyte Charles, the bass and other bands
title: Stale Bread, mandolin and banjo players, Tom Denton
summary: Dawson recalls Stale Bread's white trio in the Irish Channel, rates Big Head Sun the best mandolinist, and says Tom Denton played banjo with the Pelican band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What about Stale Bread? Did you ever hear of Stale Bread?
Yeah he's a white boy. He was from the front of town. They had a little trio I believe, a little bunch there he's playing.
Did you ever hear him with guitar playing clandery? They were not together then?

No, it was all up in that Irish Channel all the time. They never played no dances or nothing like that. That's all. Who was the best mandolin player? Big Head Sun. I had a fella, a boy called Big Head Sun. He was from downtown. He was about the best mandolin player we had. Frank, now Chicken, off the bank, he was pretty good. Then after Columbia, I was right behind sitting on a mandolin. I was a good man. I played pretty. Well could Frank Landry play mandolin? Yeah, he played. He was good.

What about that other guy out there, Dierrensberg? Caffrey Dierrensberg? Do you know him? Did you know Caffrey? Caffrey? Yeah, he played. He and Percy both played banjo. Percy, Percy Alfred? No. No, Percy Dierrensberg. Oh. There were two brothers. There was a player with you from the... Well didn't he play with... Perares. Perares at the Pythian Temple. You'd know him if you saw him. Well you wouldn't recognize him now, he's dead. Anyway... If you saw his picture, you'd know him. I'll show you his picture. And uh, what about Tom Denton? Did he play?

He played banjo. He was a good banjo player. He played with uh... with our band and the Pelican band with Edward Clemmen too, you see. Oh. Yeah. After, yeah, Edward Clemmen uh... got him on banjo and me on the bass.
But you didn't hear him on mandolin, huh?

No. I knew he could play though. Yeah. Yeah. There's so many mandolin players here. Oh yeah, we heard that's all. You see, most of the time, and a long time ago, we used to practice that, mandolin and guitar. I'd play mandolin, you'd play guitar. As long as I had compliments, you know, it was a good time. Get out on a weekend and have us a good time.
